header.name: Estimation Theory for dynamic systems
header.description:
Estimation Theory is an advanced course designed for M.Tech and PhD students. With the ever-increasing use of autonomous systems, the use of estimation algorithms to extract useful information from noisy sensor data are now almost ubiquitous. This course aims to expose students to the estimation problems in a generalized manner so that they can identify, formulate and solve estimation problems.

The course will start with an introduction to optimal linear estimation in static systems. Then continuous and discrete linear dynamic systems with random noise will be discussed. After discussing the celebrated Kalman Filter, the course will focus on estimation problems for non-linear dynamic systems. Subsequently, the Extended Kalman Filter, the Unscented Kalman Filter, and the Particle Filter will be introduced. Additionally, adaptive estimation for maneuvering targets will also be discussed.

Using MATLAB in their assignments, students will simulate dynamic systems and apply various estimation techniques in some practical problems.

outcomes.label: CO3

outcomes.label: CO4

outcomes.label: CO5

lecture_topics: Linear estimation in static systems - estimation of Gaussian random vector
Linear minimum mean square error estimator
Linear dynamic system with random inputs - Continuous-time linear stochastic dynamic system
State estimation in the discrete-time linear dynamic system - Kalman Filter
Continuous-time linear state estimation - Continuous-time Kalman-Bucy Filter
State estimation for non-linear dynamic systems - The Extended Kalman Filter
Adaptive estimation and maneuvering target - Adjusting process noise
